source.title: Information-Theoretic Trust Regions for Stochastic Gradient-Based Optimization
source.authors: Philipp Dahlinger; P. Becker; Maximilian Hüttenrauch; Gerhard Neumann

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD on natural image classification and reports settings where adaptive methods do worse, as well as a Fashion-MNIST CNN exception where Adam and AdamW are competitive. It therefore refines optimizer-generalization claims under extensively tuned recipes.
record.gate_note: Rows cover test-accuracy comparisons between arTuRO, SGD, Adam, and AdamW on natural datasets. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected generalization, large-batch effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. Figure 3 optimizer ablations concern optimization methods and test accuracy, but do not directly test one of the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out accuracy of Adam and AdamW with momentum SGD on six image-classification tasks. It bears on V4 using extensive tuning of learning rates, momentum parameters and weight decay, rather than V4's limited-tuning setting. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that arTuRO combines convergence behavior like Adam with final performance comparable to carefully tuned momentum SGD. Their experiments show SGD outperforming Adam and AdamW on five tasks, with Fashion-MNIST CNN the competitive exception.
record.recipe_differences: Optimizer-comparison study using natural-label image classification and extensive hyperparameter optimization; it compares methods rather than reproducing the claim's original interventions. All algorithms use weight decay and learning-rate schedules, and arTuRO schedules its trust-region bound.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture change the optimizer comparison: Adam and AdamW are competitive on Fashion-MNIST CNN, while SGD outperforms them on the other five tasks. The authors also report SGD is harder to tune and has unstable behavior on ResNet-34 CIFAR-10.

fits_no_version.finding: arTuRO achieves competitive final test accuracy and combines rapid convergence with performance comparable to carefully tuned momentum SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information-theoretic trust-region optimization can combine fast convergence with competitive image-classification accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: OPT2023: 15th Annual Workshop on Optimization for Machine Learning
record.problems: The reported evidence is limited to six natural-image classification experiments, with no random-label, size, batch-size, or explicit-regularization ablations relevant to the other versions. Results are after extensive hyperparameter optimization; authors note SGD is harder to tune and can be unstable. Each experiment is repeated over 10 seeds.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results left out. Figure 3 optimizer ablations compare arTuRO variants and second-order methods; these do not directly test V4's SGD-versus-adaptive-optimizer claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Limited tuning restricted to learning rates and schedules; a controlled limited-versus-broader tuning comparison; language benchmarks; switching from Adam to SGD. AdamW is compared directly, but there is no isolated intervention establishing that decoupled weight decay recovers an SGD deficit. Equal or better training performance cannot be established from the supplied text rendering of Figure 7.
Batch-size effects and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Adding or removing dropout, its dependence on training-set size, and joint removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations and comparisons with other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Training-loss comparisons accompany the held-out accuracy results and could establish whether adaptive optimizers generalize worse despite equal or better training performance. Figure 7's curves cannot be read from the supplied text; add matched training-loss rows if recoverable.

record.verdict_notes: All final accuracies and doubled standard errors match Table 1. Appendix C describes tuning all hyperparameters using 50 configurations per task and algorithm, three seeds per configuration, eight-fold cross-validation and subsequent cross-evaluation. These results do not directly reproduce the limited-tuning condition, and persistent deficits do not contradict V4's qualified statement that broader tuning can remove them.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and the coexistence of memorization with natural-label generalization.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.

The paper tests image classification, comparing Adam and AdamW with momentum SGD after extensive hyperparameter tuning. It does not test language benchmarks, limited tuning, broader tuning as a separate condition, switching from Adam to SGD, or decoupled weight decay as a recovery intervention.
Dropout is present in described CNN architectures, but the paper does not test its effect through an addition or removal comparison.
